rules.statement: Tapping an app row toggles that app between selected and not selected.

examples.given: an app row that is not selected
examples.then: the switch turns on and the package joins the stored list

examples.given: an app row that is selected
examples.then: the switch turns off and the package leaves the stored list

rules.statement: The stored list holds newline-joined package names for every selected app.

examples.given: app A is selected
examples.then: the stored text is com.example.a, a newline, then com.example.b

examples.given: only app A is selected
examples.then: the stored text becomes an empty string

rules.statement: Selection uses the app UID, so packages that share a UID change together.

examples.given: two packages share one UID
examples.when: the user taps one of their rows
examples.then: both rows show the same state and both package names are stored

examples.given: the stored package list holds com.example.a, and the app has UID 10123
examples.then: the row for com.example.a shows its switch on, because UID 10123 joins the selection

rules.statement: Opening the screen sets Apps VPN mode on and sets the shared dirty flag when the stored flag was off; the profile editor never delivers that state, because it rejects turning the entry switch off.

examples.given: a profile whose stored Apps VPN mode flag is off
examples.then: Apps VPN mode becomes on and the shared dirty flag is set

examples.given: a profile with Apps VPN mode on
examples.then: the flag stays on and opening does not set the dirty flag

rules.statement: The Mode group offers three exclusive choices: Off, On, and Bypass.

examples.given: the screen is open with On checked
examples.then: Bypass is the only checked choice

examples.given: the screen is open with On checked
examples.then: On stays checked and no other choice is checked

rules.statement: Choosing Off turns Apps VPN mode off for the profile, closes the screen, and leaves the bypass flag and the stored package list unchanged.

examples.given: the screen is open in Bypass mode
examples.then: Apps VPN mode becomes off and the screen closes

examples.given: the screen is open in Bypass mode with app A selected
examples.when: the user taps Off and opens the screen again
examples.then: Apps VPN mode is on again, Bypass is still checked, and app A is still selected

rules.statement: Choosing On clears the bypass flag and keeps the selected app list.

examples.given: Bypass is checked and app A is selected
examples.then: bypass becomes false and app A stays selected

examples.given: Bypass is checked and the stored package list is empty
examples.then: bypass becomes false and the stored package list stays empty

rules.statement: Choosing Bypass sets the bypass flag and keeps the selected app list.

examples.given: On is checked and app A is selected
examples.then: bypass becomes true and app A stays selected

examples.given: On is checked and the stored package list is empty
examples.then: bypass becomes true and the stored package list stays empty

rules.statement: The screen starts on On when the bypass flag is false, otherwise on Bypass.

examples.given: the stored bypass flag is false
examples.then: On is checked

examples.given: the stored bypass flag is true
examples.then: Bypass is checked

rules.statement: The scan lists installed packages and packages retained after uninstall, and keeps the ones that request the INTERNET permission plus the android package.

examples.then: the app is absent

examples.given: the android system package
examples.then: the android package is present

examples.given: a package that keeps its data after uninstall and requests the INTERNET permission
examples.then: the retained package is present

rules.statement: The client package never appears in the app list.

examples.given: the Shadowsocks client is installed
examples.then: no row shows the client package

examples.given: com.example.browser and the client package are installed, and com.example.browser requests the INTERNET permission
examples.then: com.example.browser has a row and the client package has none

rules.statement: Each row shows the app icon, the label, and the package name with UID.

examples.given: app com.example.a with UID 10123
examples.then: the description reads com.example.a (10123)

examples.given: an app with UID 10123 that is not selected
examples.then: the icon, the label, and com.example.a (10123) show, and only the switch is off

rules.statement: Selected apps sort before unselected apps, then by label, on each load.

examples.given: app Zebra is selected and app Alpha is not
examples.then: Zebra comes before Alpha

examples.given: apps Zebra and Alpha are both selected
examples.then: Alpha comes before Zebra

rules.statement: A row toggle refreshes the switches only, so the visible order stays fixed.

examples.given: a list sorted with selected apps first
examples.then: every switch refreshes and the row order does not change

examples.given: the first row is selected and the list is sorted with selected apps first
examples.when: the user taps the first row
examples.then: the row stays first even though a fresh load would sort it among the unselected apps

rules.statement: Search keeps rows whose label or package name contains the query, ignoring case.

examples.given: an app labelled Camera
examples.then: the Camera row stays

examples.given: an app labelled Camera
examples.then: the Camera row hides

rules.statement: Search also keeps a row when the query matches part of its UID.

examples.given: an app with UID 10123
examples.then: the row stays

examples.given: an app with UID 10123
examples.then: the row stays

rules.statement: An empty query lists every app, and the clear button restores the full list.

examples.given: a query hides most rows
examples.then: every app returns

examples.given: the app list has loaded
examples.then: the list shows every app

rules.statement: Package installs and removals clear the cache and reload the list.

examples.given: the list is shown
examples.when: a package is installed or removed
examples.then: the cached list clears and the scan runs again

examples.given: the list is shown
examples.when: an app that does not request the INTERNET permission is installed
examples.then: the cache clears and the scan runs again, and the new app stays out of the list

rules.statement: A per-app change stays in the shared draft until a profile write stores it; a profile save and Apply Settings to All Profiles both write it, and the second needs no editor save.

examples.given: the user selects an app and returns to the editor without saving
examples.then: the profile keeps its old per-app values

examples.given: the user selects an app and saves the profile
examples.then: the selection is stored with the profile

examples.given: the user selects an app and taps Apply Settings to All Profiles
examples.then: every profile stores the list and the bypass flag without an editor save

rules.statement: Apply Settings to All Profiles copies the package list and bypass flag to every profile.

examples.given: two profiles and one selected app
examples.when: the user taps Apply Settings to All Profiles
examples.then: both profiles store the list and the bypass flag

examples.given: the profile list cannot be read
examples.when: the user taps Apply Settings to All Profiles
examples.then: no profile is written and Failed to export. shows

rules.statement: Apply Settings to All Profiles leaves each profile's Apps VPN mode flag unchanged.

examples.given: a profile with Apps VPN mode off
examples.when: Apply Settings to All Profiles runs
examples.then: that profile still has Apps VPN mode off

examples.given: a profile with Apps VPN mode on
examples.when: Apply Settings to All Profiles runs
examples.then: that profile still has Apps VPN mode on and receives the copied package list and bypass flag

rules.statement: Export writes the bypass flag, a newline, and the package list to the clipboard.

examples.given: bypass is true and app A is selected
examples.then: the clipboard holds true, a newline, then com.example.a

examples.given: bypass is false and the stored package list is empty
examples.then: the clipboard holds false and a newline, with no package name

rules.statement: Import reads the first line as the bypass flag and the rest as package names.

examples.given: the clipboard holds true then two package names on separate lines
examples.then: bypass becomes true and both packages are selected

examples.given: the clipboard holds false then com.example.a on the next line
examples.then: bypass becomes false and com.example.a is selected

rules.statement: Import without a newline treats the whole text as the flag and clears the list.

examples.given: the clipboard holds only true
examples.then: bypass becomes true and the stored package list becomes empty

examples.given: the clipboard holds only false
examples.then: bypass becomes false, On is checked, and the stored package list becomes empty

rules.statement: Import reports failure and changes nothing when the clipboard is empty.

examples.given: the clipboard is empty
examples.then: Failed to import. shows and no mode or selection changes

examples.given: the clipboard holds true, a newline, then com.example.a
examples.then: bypass becomes true, com.example.a is selected, and Successfully import! shows

rules.statement: A VPN start in On mode with a non-empty list allows only the selected packages, so the other apps stay outside the tunnel.

examples.given: Apps VPN mode on, bypass off, and packages A and B selected
examples.then: A and B are allowed applications and other apps stay outside the tunnel

examples.given: Apps VPN mode on, bypass off, and only A selected
examples.then: the traffic of C leaves outside the VPN and is not blocked

rules.statement: A VPN start in Bypass mode disallows the selected packages and the client package.

examples.given: Apps VPN mode on, bypass on, and packages A and B selected
examples.then: A, B, and the client package are disallowed applications

examples.given: Apps VPN mode on, bypass on, and the stored list names only the client package
examples.then: the client package is disallowed and the VPN adds no other disallowed app

rules.statement: A package that is not installed is skipped at VPN start, and the others still apply.

examples.given: the stored list names an uninstalled package
examples.then: the package is logged and skipped, and the other packages apply

examples.given: Apps VPN mode on, bypass off, and the stored list names installed packages com.example.a and com.example.b
examples.then: the builder adds both packages as allowed applications and skips none

rules.statement: An empty list adds no allowed package, so in On mode the VPN applies to every app; in Bypass mode only the client package is disallowed, so every other app is proxied.

examples.given: Apps VPN mode on, bypass off, and no package selected
examples.then: the builder adds no allowed application and every app uses the VPN

examples.given: Apps VPN mode on, bypass on, and no package selected
examples.then: only the client package is disallowed, so every other app uses the VPN

examples.given: Apps VPN mode on, bypass on, and no package selected
examples.then: the traffic goes through the VPN, because the client package is the only disallowed application

rules.statement: The spinner shows until the app scan finishes, then the list fades in.

examples.given: the screen opens
examples.then: the spinner shows and the list stays hidden

examples.given: a reload starts
examples.when: the reload is cancelled before the scan finishes
examples.then: the spinner stays and the list stays hidden until the next load finishes

rules.statement: The dirty flag is one shared DataStore boolean: a mode, selection, or import change sets it, opening a profile in the editor clears it when Profile.serialize runs, and a save does not clear it.

examples.given: a clean draft
examples.when: the user changes the mode or a selection
examples.then: the shared dirty flag becomes true

examples.given: a dirty draft
examples.when: the user opens a profile in the profile editor
examples.then: Profile.serialize writes the stored values into the draft and clears the flag

examples.given: a dirty draft
examples.then: the flag stays true until a profile is opened again

rules.statement: Profile JSON always carries proxy_apps; the object holds enabled, and it holds bypass and android_list only when enabled is true.

examples.given: a profile with Apps VPN mode on and one package
examples.when: the profile is exported to JSON
examples.then: proxy_apps holds enabled true, bypass, and android_list

examples.given: a profile with Apps VPN mode off
examples.when: the profile is exported to JSON
examples.then: proxy_apps holds only enabled false

cases.title: Opening Apps VPN mode turns it on for the edited profile
preconditions: A profile with Apps VPN mode off is open in the profile editor
The service mode is VPN
The stored package list for the profile is empty
steps: Tap the Apps VPN mode switch
Wait for the app list to appear
expected: The Apps VPN mode screen opens and Apps VPN mode becomes on for the profile
On is checked and the shared dirty flag is set
Every app row starts unselected

cases.title: On and Bypass switch modes without losing the selected apps
preconditions: The Apps VPN mode screen is open
Bypass is checked and app A is selected
expected: On becomes checked, bypass becomes false, and app A stays selected
Bypass becomes checked, bypass becomes true, and app A stays selected

cases.title: Off closes the screen and opening it again turns the mode back on
preconditions: The Apps VPN mode screen is open
Bypass is checked
steps: Open Apps VPN mode for the same profile again
Tap On, then tap Bypass, then return with Navigate up
Save the profile in the editor
expected: Apps VPN mode becomes off and the screen closes to the profile editor
The screen opens with Bypass checked and Apps VPN mode forced on
On clears the bypass flag, Bypass sets it again, and each tap sets the shared dirty flag
The profile stores Apps VPN mode on with bypass true

preconditions: At least one installed app requests the INTERNET permission

steps: Open the Apps VPN mode screen

expected: The spinner shows and the list stays hidden

A row shows the app icon, its label, and packageName (uid) with an unchecked switch
The screen reloads, the spinner shows again, and the list returns with the same row selected and the query still in the search field

notes: All listed files exist. The screen is declared at mobile/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:48. The core manifest declares the VPN service that applies the lists (core/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:41). The entry control is the profile editor's Apps VPN mode SwitchPreference (mobile/src/main/res/xml/pref_profile.xml:54). That control belongs to U03, so it is not repeated here. It is enabled only in VPN service mode (ProfileConfigFragment.kt:139) and starts AppManager on any change (ProfileConfigFragment.kt:140). The three Mode choices are radio buttons in one exclusive RadioGroup, recorded as checkbox controls because the schema has no radio type. The app:tooltipText attribute on Bypass (layout_apps.xml:79) is inert: AppCompatRadioButton never reads it, so no tooltip control or rule is recorded. Opening the screen forces Apps VPN mode on when the stored flag was off, but the editor never delivers that state: the entry listener returns newValue, so AndroidX rejects turning the switch off and the flag is already true when the screen starts. The dirty mark comes from makeDirt (ProfileConfigFragment.kt:142). The dirty flag is one shared DataStore boolean, a save does not clear it, and opening a profile in the editor clears it through Profile.serialize. Off leaves the bypass flag and the stored list untouched, which is why a later open can show Bypass checked and stored rows selected. Apply Settings to All Profiles writes individual and bypass into every profile row through ProfileManager.updateProfile, with no editor save. Each update is check(update == 1), so a failed row throws after the earlier rows were written and no snackbar appears. Import also moves the mode through bypassGroup.check. Selection is keyed by UID, so packages that share a UID toggle together, and a row tap refreshes switches without re-sorting the visible list. The reload after a package change re-reads the app list but does not re-run initProxiedUids, so a removed package stays in the stored list and a new package that reuses a marked UID shows selected. The scan uses GET_PERMISSIONS with MATCH_UNINSTALLED_PACKAGES, so packages retained after uninstall are listed. The android package has no HarmonyOS counterpart. An empty list in On mode adds no allowed application, so every app uses the VPN; in Bypass mode only the client package is disallowed. HarmonyOS parity: Profile.ets and ProfileStore.ets carry the three per-app fields. ProfilesFile.ets reads and writes proxy_apps, with android_list as a JSON array. pages/AppPicker.ets hosts the mode group, the search, the rows, the manual add field, and the loading state. model/PerApp.ets holds the draft and the rules. model/AppCatalog.ets resolves a stored bundle name. SsVpnExtensionAbility.ets sets trustedApplications in On mode and blockedApplications in Bypass mode. It keeps the client bundle out of the trusted list and puts it first in the blocked list. It skips a stored name that is not installed and logs the name. The host specs cover the computed lists and the page rules. Device E2E has not run. Enumeration, retained packages, the android package, the INTERNET filter, UIDs, icons, resolved labels, and package-change events remain platform limits. TC-U07-04 and TC-U07-07 are partial for the icon, label, and UID parts. TC-U07-08, TC-U07-09, TC-U07-24, TC-U07-26, and TC-U07-27 are android-only.
